memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Elena developed a two-person May 1-3 wedding itinerary from Denver to Raleigh. She selected the earlier Friday nonstop and Sunday afternoon nonstop in standard economy, chose one king room at the Longleaf, and plans to use rideshares rather than rent a car. Nothing was booked. The Sunday brunch location, Saturday-night transportation arrangement, final prices, hotel terms, and seat availability remain to be confirmed.

messages.content: I need to start a separate trip for my niece's wedding near Raleigh on Saturday, May 2. My spouse and I will fly from Denver on Friday, stay two nights in one room, and come home Sunday.

What time is the family dinner on Friday, and where are the dinner and wedding being held? Those details will determine how late you can arrive and whether downtown Raleigh or a hotel closer to the ceremony makes more sense.
Dinner is at 7:00 Friday evening near Glenwood South. The wedding is at 4:30 Saturday at Chatham Station in Cary. There is no hotel shuttle or wedding transportation.

Then I would target an RDU arrival by about 3:30 p.m. Friday. That leaves time to collect bags, reach downtown, and check in before dinner. For Sunday, do you have a preferred departure window, and will either of you need to check a bag?
Sunday afternoon would be best. We will probably check one suitcase between us. Please compare nonstop flights first, but include a connection if it saves a meaningful amount.

A representative nonstop combination is an 8:05 a.m. Friday departure from Denver, arriving at RDU around 1:25 p.m., with a Sunday return leaving near 4:05 p.m. and reaching Denver around 6:05 p.m. The current standard-economy estimate is about $898 total for two, plus any checked-bag charge. A lower fare around $778 total is basic economy and is less flexible.

A connecting option through Atlanta is roughly $690 total, but it arrives close to 4:40 p.m. Friday. That is too exposed to a missed dinner if either segment slips, so I would not use it for this schedule.
Agreed. Is there another nonstop that is a little later Friday morning without getting us in too close to dinner?

There is a nonstop around 10:20 a.m. that reaches Raleigh at approximately 3:40 p.m. It gives you about three hours and twenty minutes before dinner. Under ordinary traffic that is workable, but checked baggage and Friday congestion would reduce the margin. It is currently about $936 total for two in standard economy, roughly $38 more than the earlier pairing.
The earlier one sounds safer. What does the hotel picture look like downtown compared with Cary?

For one room from Friday to Sunday, three plausible examples are:

The Longleaf Hotel, just north of downtown: approximately $421 including taxes for a king room. It is a short rideshare from Glenwood South and has free parking if you rent a car.

Raleigh Marriott City Center: approximately $536 including taxes for a king room. It is central and full service, but overnight parking is about $30 per night.

A comparable hotel near central Cary: approximately $338 including taxes. It is convenient for Saturday's wedding but about 20 to 30 minutes from Friday dinner and farther from the downtown family activity.

The downtown options make Friday easier; Cary saves around $80 to $200 on lodging.
Some relatives are having brunch downtown Sunday, although we do not have the restaurant yet. That probably argues against Cary.

Yes. With both Friday dinner and Sunday brunch downtown, staying in Raleigh avoids moving back and forth for two of the three scheduled events. You would only need a round trip to Cary for the wedding. The Longleaf is the lower-cost downtown choice, while the Marriott is more central for walking but costs about $115 more before its parking charge.
Can you compare renting a car for the whole weekend with using rideshares?

An airport rental from Friday afternoon through Sunday afternoon is currently around $184 including estimated taxes for a compact car, before fuel. At the Longleaf, parking is included; at the Marriott, two nights of parking would bring the transportation total to roughly $244 plus fuel.

Estimated rideshares are $25 to $35 from RDU to downtown, $30 to $45 each way between downtown and Chatham Station, and $25 to $35 back to RDU. That puts the likely weekend total around $110 to $160, with possible event or surge pricing. Rideshares are probably cheaper for this itinerary, especially with the Longleaf, though the Saturday return should be requested early because several wedding guests may leave together.
Would it be awkward to get a ride from Chatham Station late Saturday? The reception ends around 10:30.

It should be possible, but I would not depend on finding a car instantly at 10:30. Cary has regular rideshare coverage, and the venue is not remote, but reception-end demand can create a wait. Scheduling a pickup in advance for about 10:40 or arranging to share a ride with relatives would reduce that risk. A rental car offers more certainty but also means one of you cannot drink and must handle parking.
Let's stay downtown and use rideshares. Between the Longleaf and the Marriott, which works better if we have luggage after Sunday checkout?

Both should be able to hold luggage for registered guests after checkout, but that service should be confirmed with the reservation. The Marriott has the advantage if brunch is in the central business district because you could retrieve the bag without another ride. The Longleaf is still only a short ride away, and its approximately $115 room savings would cover that extra trip several times over.
Use the Longleaf in the working plan. One king room is fine. We do not need separate beds.

The working combination is now the early Friday nonstop, the Sunday afternoon nonstop, one king room at the Longleaf for Friday and Saturday nights, and rideshares for airport transfers and the Cary wedding. The estimated base is about $1,319 for flights and hotel, before the checked bag, rideshares, and any hotel incidental hold.
Can you give me a fuller trip estimate? I want to see whether the cheaper flight fare is actually worth considering.

Using the standard-economy flights, the planning estimate is:

Flights for two: about $898.
Hotel for two nights including estimated tax: about $421.
One checked suitcase round trip: allow roughly $70 to $80, depending on the airline and whether it is prepaid.
Four primary rideshare legs: allow $140, including some cushion for Saturday night.

That produces an estimated trip total of about $1,529 to $1,539, excluding meals.

Basic economy would lower the airfare by about $120 total, bringing the trip estimate to roughly $1,409 to $1,419. The tradeoff is tighter change and cancellation rules, later seat assignment or paid seat selection, and potentially less predictable seating for the two of you.
We would rather sit together, and I do not want this wedding trip made difficult over $120. Keep standard economy. Can we take two aisle seats across from each other if adjacent seats are limited?

Yes. For two travelers, adjacent aisle and middle seats are usually the simplest way to remain together, but two aisle seats across the same row are a reasonable alternative if available. Seat selection and any fee should be checked before purchase because the displayed standard fare may not include every preferred seat.
Please finish with the exact working request, but do not book anything yet. Also note that the brunch location and final wedding pickup arrangement are still unknown.

Working request only, with no booking authorization: two travelers from Denver to Raleigh-Durham for the May 2 wedding. Depart Denver Friday, May 1 on the approximately 8:05 a.m. nonstop, arriving around 1:25 p.m. Return Sunday, May 3 on the approximately 4:05 p.m. nonstop, arriving in Denver around 6:05 p.m. Price standard economy for both travelers, include one shared checked suitcase, and seek either adjacent seats or two aisle seats across the same row.

Lodging: one king room for two guests at the Longleaf Hotel, check-in May 1 and check-out May 3, currently estimated at $421 including taxes. Confirm the final taxed total, cancellation deadline, deposit terms, and post-checkout luggage storage before reserving.

Use rideshares between RDU and downtown and for the Saturday round trip to Chatham Station in Cary. The Friday dinner begins at 7:00 p.m. near Glenwood South, and the wedding begins at 4:30 p.m. Saturday. Sunday brunch location and the Saturday 10:40 p.m. pickup or family ride arrangement remain unresolved. Current total estimate is approximately $1,529 to $1,539 before meals. Flight schedules, fares, room availability, and fees must be reconfirmed before purchase.
